name: Krati
tagline: LinkedIn's hash-based persistent key-value store for the JVM, tuned for low latency and little GC.
description: Krati is a Java library from LinkedIn's Search, Network and Analytics (SNA) team, released in 2010. It offers array-style stores keyed by integer index and hash-based stores for arbitrary byte keys, writing values into segment files and relying on periodic checkpoints for durability. The pitch was very low latency and high throughput for read-write-heavy services with little effort spent on configuration, performance tuning or JVM garbage collection, and a krati-avro module added Avro-serialized stores. The last release, 0.4.9, came out in February 2013 and the repository has been dormant since.
statusNote: No commits since Sept 2013; last release 0.4.9 (Feb 2013). For embedded JVM key-value storage use RocksDB (RocksJava), LMDB or MapDB.

scale.notes: Single-JVM library; sharding is up to the application.

strengths: Low, predictable latency for read-write-heavy JVM workloads
Minimal tuning and little garbage-collection pressure
Simple array and hash store abstractions with Avro support
weaknesses: No transactions, range scans or secondary indexes
Durability limited to checkpoints and segment logs
useCases: Studying segment-log plus memory-mapped index designs
Legacy JVM services that still embed it
notIdealFor: New projects (choose RocksDB, LMDB or MapDB)
Workloads needing ordered scans or transactions
